title: The knight
summary: The knight jumps in an L-shape and is the only piece that can leap over others. Learn its move and why it hates the corner.

steps.title: The L-shaped jump
steps.text: The knight moves in an L: two squares in one direction, then one square to the side. From d4 it can land on any of the eight circled squares. Notice that it always lands on a square of the opposite color to the one it started on.
steps.narration: The knight is the odd one out. It moves in an L shape: two squares one way, then one square to the side. From the middle of the board it has eight places to land.

steps.title: Jumping over pieces
steps.text: The knight is the only piece that can jump. Pieces in between do not block it; only the landing square matters. That is why a knight can move on the very first turn, hopping right over its own pawns.
steps.narration: Here's the knight's superpower: it can jump. At the very start of the game, it hops right over the pawns. [move] Nothing in between can block it.

steps.title: Knights hate corners
steps.text: A knight in the corner reaches only two squares, compared with eight in the center. Players say a knight on the rim is dim. Keep your knights near the middle of the board, where they control the most squares.
steps.narration: Poor knight. Stuck in the corner, it can only reach two squares. Remember this one: a knight on the rim is dim. Bring your knights toward the center.

steps.title: Catch the intruder
steps.prompt: Black's rook has invaded your second rank. Capture it with the knight.
steps.hint: Count two squares one way and one square to the side from b1.
steps.success: Knight to d2 takes the rook. Black's rook was attacking your pawns, and now it's gone.
steps.narration: A black rook has crashed into your camp on d2. Your knight on b1 is close by. Can you see the L-shaped jump that captures it?

steps.title: Which capture is free?
steps.prompt: Your knight can capture the bishop on c5 or the pawn on f6. Take the free one.
steps.hint: Which of the two is protected by a pawn?
steps.success: The bishop had no defender, so you won a piece. On f6 your knight would have been taken by the g7 pawn.
steps.narration: Your knight can capture two things. The pawn on f6 gives check, but look who protects it. The bishop on c5, on the other hand, is all alone.

steps.title: Quick check
steps.question: Which of these is true about the knight?

options.text: It can jump over other pieces
options.why: The knight is the only piece that jumps. Only its landing square has to be free of your own pieces.

options.text: It is strongest in the corner
options.why: In the corner it reaches only two squares. In the center it reaches eight.

options.text: It moves in a straight line
options.why: That is the rook. The knight moves in an L: two squares, then one to the side.

steps.narration: Final question about the knight. Which of these statements is true?
